Elena: Quick follow-up on fragmentation: proposing a compact-priority abstraction instead of boolean pin. Idea: presets (StickyHot, AdvisoryHot, ArchiveCold) mapped to an internal 0-100 compact_priority. Keeps SDK surface small but gives runtime fine-grained scoring.

Marco: Love the mapping. Show the minimal API?

Elena: ```c
// alloc2(owner, size, preset)
enum Preset { StickyHot, AdvisoryHot, ArchiveCold }
// internal: preset -> compact_priority (StickyHot=90, AdvisoryHot=45, ArchiveCold=5)
```

Priya: Two operational rules to avoid runaway frag: 1) demotion-grace default 36h for StickyHot, 2) a compaction token-bucket that gates background compaction based on current inference load.

Vik: Add KV-affinity flag. If alloc is tied to KV entries, bump compact_priority +15. Also prefer host-compress instead of spill to reduce IO during demote.

Sahil: Need telemetry before enabling: alloc_hint{preset,tenant,outcome}, fragmentation_index{tenant,window}, compaction_tokens_util. Also trace compaction start/stop.

Elena: Rollout: telemetry-only -> soft-apply (advisory) -> tenant-enforce. Each stage 2 weeks with canary monitoring. If p99 latency >10% or fragmentation_index up >15%, auto rollback.

Marco: For compaction algorithm: only compact on nodes with low active inference (query local load signals), and limit bytes/sec via token-bucket proportional to spare GPU cycles.

Priya: I'll prototype a demote worker that marks candidates sticky->archive when idle > grace and only moves to host-compress. It will compute expected fragmentation delta heuristically before acting.

Vik: Let's hide numeric 0-100 API from public SDKs; expose only presets. Keep numeric available to ops CLI for emergency tuning.

ops-bot: deploy-signal: canary/alloc2-telemetry passed 2026-03-22T09:11:00Z

Elena: Great. I'll update RFC: presets, demote heuristics, compaction-throttle pseudo, KV-affinity, telemetry schema, rollout plan, and ops playbook for force-demote and emergency compaction. PR by EOD.
